name: Linnorm, Young
body:
YOUNG LINNORM
CR 7

This serpentine dragon is the young version of the more terrifying linnorms you normally see.

XP 3,200
CE Large dragon
Init +10; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 24, touch 13, flat-footed 20 (+4 Dex, +11 natural, -1 size)
hp 94 (9d12+36); regeneration 5 (cold iron)
Fort +13, Ref +13, Will +11
Defensive Abilities DR 10/cold iron; Immune curse effects, mindaffecting effects, paralysis, poison, sleep; SR 18

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 60 ft. (average)
Melee bite +19 (1d10+5/19-20 plus poison), 2 claws +19 (1d8+5), tail +14 (1d8+2 plus grab)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks constrict (tail, 1d8+7)

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 18, Con 18, Int 5, Wis 15, Cha 19
Base Atk +9; CMB +15 (+19 grapple); CMD 29 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Combat Reflexes, Improved Critical (bite), Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack
Skills Fly +8, Perception +8, Swim +19
Languages Aklo, Draconic, Sylvan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 18; frequency 1/round for 10 rounds; effect depends upon linnorm type below; cure 2 consecutive saves.

Changes Based on Linnorm Type
Cairn–Immune to acid; climb speed 30 ft.; poison effect: 2d6 acid damage and 1d4 Con damage
Crag–Immune to fire; swim speed 40 ft.; poison effect: 1d6 fire damage and 1d4 Con damage
Fjord–Immune to cold; swim speed 40 ft.; poison effect: 2d6 cold damage and 1d4 Con damage; gain aquatic subtype
Gare–Immune to fire; swim speed 40 ft. no fly speed; poison effect: 2d6 fire damage and 1d4 Dex damage; gain aquatic subtype
Ice–Immune to cold; swim speed 40 ft., climb speed 30 ft.; poison effect: 2d6 cold damage and 1d4 Con damage; gain aquatic subtype
Sea–Immune to electricity; swim speed 40 ft.; poison effect: 2d6 electricity damage and 1d2 Con damage, 1d2 Dex damage; gain aquatic subtype
Shoal–Immune to fire; swim speed 40 ft.; poison effect: 2d6 fire damage and 1d4 Con damage; gain aquatic subtype
Taiga–Immune to electricity; swim speed 40 ft.; poison effect: 2d6 electricity damage and 1d4 Dex damage
Tarn–Immune to acid; swim speed 40 ft.; poison effect: 2d6 acid damage and 1d4 Con damage
Tor–Immune to fire; swim speed 40 ft., climb speed 30 ft.; poison effect: 2d6 fire damage and 1d4 Con damage

ECOLOGY

Environment varies based on linnorm type
Organization solitary
Treasure triple

Female linnorms lay eggs in the wilderness, where linnorms are known to hunt. A linnorm egg remains viable for many years, protected by a tough, leathery skin easily mistaken for stone. When a male linnorm eventually stumbles across the egg, he fertilizes it and takes it to a secure and remote location, leaving it alone to eventually hatch. Newborn linnorms remain hidden in their nests for several months as they mature, growing large enough to hunt on their own and setting out into the world. These linnorms are roughly the equivalent of older teenagers when compared to other species. Younger linnorms, while still primal creatures with a strong tie to the First World, haven’t yet manifested most of their magical powers. They still can’t breathe deadly fire or lightning or see invisible creatures, and, most importantly, they can be slain without prompting the linnorm’s legendary death curse. They do, however, have voracious appetites, consuming any living thing to fuel their rapid growth. A linnorm is most vulnerable during this time; scouts who find tracks of a young linnorm quickly muster a hunting party of stalwart and experienced warriors to track the creature down and kill it quickly—before they draw the attention of the linnorm’s father.

Linnorms grow quickly, they are born in the state above and after 3 months they grow larger gaining the advanced template, and the true seeing and freedom of movement abilities of larger linnorms. After 1 full year of life, they reach adulthood and turn into a normal linnorm of their type. These linnorms, while still powerful, are more likely to get a boastful warrior laughed out of town rather than crowned a “linnorm king.”
